meta.description: Crystal-field parameters B_k^q (cm^-1) and ground-manifold level energies (cm^-1) of the C3-symmetric Er(III) single-ion magnet Er-trensal (compound 1 of the paper), in three electronic-structure columns. Known-answer data for the A4 crystal-field fitter: the nine non-zero B_k^q are exactly the (k, q) set allowed by a true three-fold axis, the eight energies are the Kramers-doublet levels of the fitted Hamiltonian.
meta.source: Peng L., Liu S., Zhang X., Chen X., Li C., Ung S. F., Cheng H.-P., Chan G. K.-L., Accurate Crystal Field Hamiltonians of Single-Ion Magnets at Mean-Field Cost, J. Phys. Chem. Lett., 2025, 16(47), 12312-12320, DOI 10.1021/acs.jpclett.5c02971
tables: Supporting Information, Table S1 (B_k^q, three columns)
Supporting Information, Table S6 (Kramers-doublet level energies, two columns)
meta.transcription_note: Values transcribed from our reading notes (close-reading file) of the paper, 文献细读/细读_CF哈密顿量_Chan2025.md section 4.6, which quotes the SI tables of both the journal version and the arXiv preprint (arXiv:2505.16905v2); the two conversions of Table S1 agree row by row. Not read from the PDF figure.
meta.level_convention: Level 1 is the ground Kramers doublet and is set to 0; the eight tabulated energies are the doubly-degenerate levels of the J = 15/2 (Er3+, 4I15/2) manifold. They are levels, not sampled-state energies: the fitter needs one energy per sampled state plus the projection coefficients of that state (see tests/test_crystal_field.py).
meta.operator_convention: Extended Stevens operators of the Rudowicz/Ryabov lineage, extended (cosine/sine) form; q = +3 and q = -3 are independent parameters, which is why both appear below. B_k^q in cm^-1. z axis: pseudo-C3 axis of the molecule. The paper's own footnote states that the CASPT2 column is given in the coordinate frame used for the two other columns.
meta.warning: B_k^q from a different operator convention, manifold, unit or z-axis are not comparable with these numbers.

parameters.zero_parameters: All other (k, q) with k in {2, 4, 6} are zero in the two mean-field columns; the CASPT2 column has residual values of order 1e-3 to 1e-8 (paper, Table S1).

levels.note: The paper's own convergence statement: the mean-field spectrum is not an eigenstate sample. Comparing a fitted CF Hamiltonian against these levels is step 6 of the paper's workflow.

cross_check.method: Build H_CF from the nine B_k^q of a column, diagonalise, subtract the ground level, and compare the eight Kramers doublets with the same column of Table S6. Measured 2026-09-25 with this module's operators, J = 15/2, basis |J M>.
cross_check.PBE0@HF: Reproduces Table S6 to max |deviation| = 0.0039 cm^-1, i.e. within the 0.01 cm^-1 to which the table is printed. This is an external known-answer test of the operator normalisation and of the cosine/sine phase convention.
cross_check.HF@HF: Reproduces Table S6 only up to a constant factor: the diagonalised spectrum is 0.7633557 x the tabulated levels (least-squares factor over the seven excited doublets; the per-level ratio scatters by only 2.9e-5, which is the table's own rounding). The reciprocal 1.3100053 is confirmed to five digits, and the same factor recurs in the HF@HF column of compound 5 (1.3099995, re-checked 2026-09-26), so it is a systematic undeclared rescaling of the HF@HF level columns, not a one-off. It is not a unit conversion (no cm^-1-to-K/meV/GHz factor matches) and not an operator or normalisation convention (the PBE0@HF column reproduces exactly under the same operators, and a convention error cannot leave a factor that is constant to 1e-5). The authors' code repository (github.com/penglinq/cDFT-CF, stevens/cf_parameter.py) builds both tables from the same fitted object, and its example output reproduces the PBE0@HF column of Table S7 verbatim, so the factor can only come from data handling on the HF@HF side. Both tables were re-read verbatim from the SI conversion text (jz5c02971_si_001.md) and the PDF text layer to rule out a transcription error on our side; the nine B_k^q and the eight levels match that text exactly.
cross_check.consequence: Use the PBE0@HF pair (B_k^q and levels) as the known answer; the compound 3 and compound 4 pairs also reproduce to max 0.005 cm^-1 (2026-09-26 check), and the Oh pair (compound 2) exactly. The HF@HF column of Table S6 must not be paired with the HF@HF column of Table S1 without the 1.3100 factor, and the two sides must not be mixed across tables; the factor is recorded as an undeclared rescaling (erratum-like). The paper's separate empirical factor of 1.3 on its CASSCF(7o) spectrum of compound 5 is a different object, distinguishable from 1.3100 at the quoted precision.

round_trip_note: Round-trip recipe used in the tests: build H_CF from one column of the nine B_k^q, diagonalise it, and feed the 16 eigenpairs back into fit_crystal_field. On its own this recovers nothing -- the Kramers doublets duplicate the design-matrix rows (measured rank 8 of 10 columns). Adding oriented sampled states restores full rank and the nine B_k^q come back to ~1e-12 relative.
